label: W01 Timber frame insulated wall

auditNote: Framing fraction changes the U-factor. The listed value assumes 75% insulated cavity and 25% wood framing.

label: W02 Light-gauge steel-frame wall
thicknessSummary: board 13 mm + insulation 90 mm + board 13 mm
optionLabel: Steel wall (inside board 13 mm + wall insulation 90 mm + inside board 13 mm)

auditNote: Metal thermal bridging controls this wall. Product or tested assembly U-factor should replace the example value when available.

label: W03 Concrete sandwich wall with 50 mm extruded polystyrene insulation
thicknessSummary: concrete 80 mm + insulation 50 mm + concrete 120 mm
optionLabel: Concrete wall (concrete 80 mm + middle insulation 50 mm + concrete 120 mm)

label: W04 Reinforced concrete frame with 200 mm cement block infill
thicknessSummary: plaster 20 mm + block 200 mm + plaster 20 mm
optionLabel: Cement block wall (concrete frame + plaster 20 mm + cement block 200 mm + plaster 20 mm)

auditNote: Reinforced concrete columns and beams are separate thermal bridges; the listed value is for the cement block infill path.

label: W05 200 mm autoclaved aerated concrete block wall with plaster
thicknessSummary: plaster 20 mm + block 200 mm + plaster 20 mm
optionLabel: Light concrete block wall (plaster 20 mm + block 200 mm + plaster 20 mm)

auditNote: Use manufacturer conductivity for the selected autoclaved aerated concrete product when available.

label: W06 Double-leaf brick cavity wall

auditNote: Cavity width and ties vary by practice; the listed air-space resistance is the Table 3 20 mm vertical nonreflective case.

label: W07 Brick wall with 50 mm external expanded polystyrene insulation

label: W08 100 mm insulated metal sandwich panel
uFactorBasis: Idealized one-dimensional panel path uses 100 mm polyisocyanurate core; metal skin resistance is neglected.
auditNote: Chapter 24 warns ribs and stiffeners create complicated heat paths. Use tested panel U-factor for precision.

label: W09 Curtain wall or glazed facade
uFactorBasis: Table 4 provides only architectural glass resistance for this path.
auditNote: Curtain walls are fenestration systems. Use glass/frame U-factor and solar inputs instead of an opaque-wall option.
